Yes — `game/domain/` is the entity layer. It holds the entities (domain model) and nothing that depends on outside layers:

- **Entities**: `GameState` (the `CommonUser`-style root entity, built via `GameStateFactory`), `Board`, `Mark`, `Position`, `GameConfig`, `GameStatus` + sealed variants (`InProgress`, `Win`, `Draw`)
- **Pure domain logic**: `WinChecker`, `LineGenerator` (helpers that serve the entities)
- **Domain values/enums**: `GameMode`, `AiDifficulty`, exceptions

Note the deliberate naming clash: the presentation bean `game.GameState` is *not* an entity — it's the view-model state living in `game/`, while the entity is `game.domain.GameState` (fully qualified inside the bean).

+Yes — `game/domain/` is the entity layer. It holds the entities (domain model) and nothing that depends on outside layers:
+
+- **Entities**: `GameState` (the `CommonUser`-style root entity, built via `GameStateFactory`), `Board`, `Mark`, `Position`, `GameConfig`, `GameStatus` + sealed variants (`InProgress`, `Win`, `Draw`)
+- **Pure domain logic**: `WinChecker`, `LineGenerator` (helpers that serve the entities)
+- **Domain values/enums**: `GameMode`, `AiDifficulty`, exceptions
+
+Note the deliberate naming clash: the presentation bean `game.GameState` is *not* an entity — it's the view-model state living in `game/`, while the entity is `game.domain.GameState` (fully qualified inside the bean).

### 1. AppBuilder has no per-frame wiring methods — everything is in one `build()`

Fields hold the views/view-models; each `add*UseCase()` constructs Presenter → Interactor → Controller and calls `view.setXController(...)`.
- Target: `/Users/pgries/Projects/ca_examples/tictactoe/src/main/java/app/AppBuilder.java` has only `build()`; everything is local to that method, only `gameViewModel` is a field, and it returns the concrete `MainFrame` subclass. This contradicts the "per-frame wiring methods" convention in AGENTS.md.

### 2. Controllers are not thin — they hold extra dependencies and mutate session state
- Reference: all three controllers (`SignupController`, `LoginController`, `ChangePasswordController` in `account/*/` and `authentication/login/`) take **only** the `InputBoundary` and only build `InputData` from primitives.
- Target: controllers take extra collaborators and do use-case work before calling the interactor:
  - `game/start_new_game/StartNewGameController.java` — takes `AiStrategyFactory` + `GameViewModel`, sets `mode`/`aiStrategy` on the shared `GameState`, and caches `lastInput` for `restart()`.
  - `game/make_human_move/MakeHumanMoveController.java` — takes `GameViewModel` and performs the game-over / AI-turn guard (use-case policy) in the controller.
  - `game/request_ai_move/RequestAiMoveController.java` — takes `GameViewModel` + `UiScheduler`, sets `pendingAiBase`, and runs the interactor on a background thread.

### 3. Strategy/factory instantiation point: controller-held factory + strategy smuggled via InputData, vs interactor-injected factory
- Reference: `user/CommonUserFactory.java` implements `UserFactory`; the AppBuilder creates it and injects it into the **interactor constructor** (`account/signup/use_case/SignupInteractor.java` calls `userFactory.create(...)`).
- Target: `game/ai/AiStrategyFactory.java` is injected into `StartNewGameController` (not the interactor), and the resulting `AiStrategy` is stored in the shared presentation bean and later passed into the use case through `game/request_ai_move/use_case/RequestAiMoveInputData.java` (record carrying `AiStrategy`). The interactors never see the factory. In the reference, external collaborators enter the use case via constructor injection at the boundary, not via input data.

### 4. Presentation bean holds domain types; class-name collision `GameState`
- Reference: per-use-case state beans (`account/signup/SignupState.java`, `authentication/login/LoginState.java`, `account/change_password/ChangePasswordState.java`) hold **only view primitives** (Strings, errors); the domain entity is `user/User.java` — clearly separated.
- Target: `game/GameState.java` (presentation) holds the domain aggregate `game.domain.GameState` plus `game.ai.AiStrategy`, and `game/GameState.java` vs `game/domain/GameState.java` are two classes with the same name in sibling packages — confusing in teaching. The presentation layer here reaches directly into domain types.

### 5. No ViewManager / ViewManagerModel; navigation is view-driven instead of presenter-driven
- Reference: `framework/ViewManager.java` (a `PropertyChangeListener` on the `ViewManagerModel` that switches a `CardLayout`) and `framework/ViewManagerModel.java` (`extends ViewModel<String>`). Presenters navigate by `viewManagerModel.setState(<viewName>)` + `firePropertyChanged()` (e.g. `SignupPresenter.prepareSuccessView`). Views expose `getViewName()`.
- Target: no ViewManager or ViewManagerModel anywhere. `framework/ui/MainFrame.java` owns a private `CardLayout` with hard-coded card names, and navigation happens when `SetupPanel.onStartClicked()` calls `mainFrame.showGameScreen()` directly — the view controls navigation, and `StartNewGamePresenter` never navigates.

### 6. `framework/ViewModel` base is missing the `firePropertyChanged(String)` overload
- Reference: `/Users/pgries/Projects/ca_examples/CAWithBuilder/src/main/java/framework/ViewModel.java` has both `firePropertyChanged()` and `firePropertyChanged(String propertyName)`; `ChangePasswordPresenter` fires `"password"` and `ChangePasswordView.propertyChange` distinguishes events by name.
- Target: `/Users/pgries/Projects/ca_examples/tictactoe/src/main/java/framework/ViewModel.java` has only the no-arg version. Also, the `viewName` field is vestigial — `MainFrame` never calls `getViewName()`.

### 7. Views live in `framework/ui`; no per-capability View classes
- Reference: one View per capability inside the capability package — `account/signup/SignupView.java`, `authentication/login/LoginView.java`, `account/change_password/ChangePasswordView.java` — each a `JPanel` implementing `PropertyChangeListener` with `getViewName()` and `setXController(...)`; only shared Swing widgets (`framework/LabelTextPanel.java`) sit in `framework`.
- Target: all UI is in `framework/ui/` (`MainFrame.java`, `SetupPanel.java`, `BoardPanel.java`, `StatusPanel.java`, `EffectOverlayPanel.java`, `Theme.java`); the per-capability View layer is absent and the capability packages contain only Controller/Presenter. AppBuilder wires via `frame.setControllers(...)` instead of per-view `setXController(...)`.

### 8. `Main` placement and content differ
- Reference: `/Users/pgries/Projects/ca_examples/CAWithBuilder/src/main/java/app/Main.java` — in the `app` package, chains `add*View()/add*UseCase()`, then `pack()` + `setVisible(true)`, no EDT wrapper.
- Target: `/Users/pgries/Projects/ca_examples/tictactoe/src/main/java/framework/Main.java` — in `framework`, uses `SwingUtilities.invokeLater` and never calls `pack()` (size is fixed in the `MainFrame` constructor). Entry point in the framework layer vs the app layer.

### 9. No per-use-case data-access interface / `data_access` layer
- Reference: each use_case package includes a DAO interface (`SignupUserDataAccessInterface`, `LoginUserDataAccessInterface`, `ChangePasswordUserDataAccessInterface`) and `data_access/` holds implementations (`DBUserDataAccessObject`, `FileUserDataAccessObject`, `InMemoryUserDataAccessObject`); AppBuilder constructs one DAO and shares it across interactors.
- Target: no DAO interfaces in the `use_case` packages and no `data_access` package at all (the game has nothing to persist, but the reference's "sixth boundary member + separate implementation layer" pattern is absent and should at least be acknowledged in teaching).

### 10. Domain entity/factory pattern: concrete classes + static factory vs interface + injectable factory
- Reference: `user/User.java` (interface), `user/UserFactory.java` (interface), `user/CommonUser.java`, `user/CommonUserFactory.java` — the "CommonUser/CommonUserFactory" pattern from AGENTS.md, instantiated in AppBuilder and injected.

- Reference: `SignupInputData`, `SignupOutputData`, etc. are plain classes with getters (some package-private, e.g. `getUsername()` in `SignupInputData`).
- Target: all six data objects are Java records with public accessors and value semantics (`StartNewGameInputData`, `MakeHumanMoveInputData`, `RequestAiMoveInputData`, and the three OutputData records).

- **Interactor construction**: both projects pass the `OutputBoundary` to the interactor **in the constructor** — no setter in the reference (`new SignupInteractor(dao, outputBoundary, factory)`, `new LoginInteractor(dao, outputBoundary)`).

```java
package app;

import game.GameViewModel;
import game.ai.AiStrategyFactory;
import game.make_human_move.MakeHumanMoveController;
import game.make_human_move.MakeHumanMovePresenter;
import game.make_human_move.use_case.MakeHumanMoveInteractor;
import game.request_ai_move.RequestAiMoveController;
import game.request_ai_move.RequestAiMovePresenter;
import game.request_ai_move.use_case.RequestAiMoveInteractor;
import game.start_new_game.StartNewGameController;
import game.start_new_game.StartNewGamePresenter;
import game.start_new_game.use_case.StartNewGameInteractor;
import framework.ui.EffectOverlayPanel;
import framework.ui.MainFrame;
import framework.ui.SwingUiScheduler;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.function.BooleanSupplier;
import javax.swing.JFrame;

public class AppBuilder {

    private final GameViewModel gameViewModel = new GameViewModel();
    private final SwingUiScheduler uiScheduler = new SwingUiScheduler();

    private MainFrame frame;
    private RequestAiMoveController requestAiMoveController;

    public AppBuilder addGameView() {
        frame = new MainFrame(gameViewModel);

        final EffectOverlayPanel effects = new EffectOverlayPanel();
        frame.setGlassPane(effects);
        effects.setVisible(true);
        frame.setWinEffects(List.of(
                ifEnabled(frame.setupPanel()::isConfettiEffectEnabled, effects::playConfetti),
                ifEnabled(frame.setupPanel()::isFireworksEffectEnabled, effects::playFireworks),
                ifEnabled(frame.setupPanel()::isMarksEffectEnabled, effects::playMarks)));
        return this;
    }

    public AppBuilder addStartNewGameUseCase() {
        final StartNewGamePresenter startNewGamePresenter = new StartNewGamePresenter(gameViewModel);
        final StartNewGameController startNewGameController = new StartNewGameController(
                new StartNewGameInteractor(startNewGamePresenter),
                new AiStrategyFactory(), gameViewModel);
        frame.setStartNewGameController(startNewGameController);
        return this;
    }

    public AppBuilder addMakeHumanMoveUseCase() {
        final MakeHumanMovePresenter makeHumanMovePresenter =
                new MakeHumanMovePresenter(gameViewModel, requestAiMoveController::execute);
        final MakeHumanMoveController makeHumanMoveController = new MakeHumanMoveController(
                new MakeHumanMoveInteractor(makeHumanMovePresenter), gameViewModel);
        frame.setMakeHumanMoveController(makeHumanMoveController);
        return this;
    }

    public AppBuilder addRequestAiMoveUseCase() {
        final RequestAiMovePresenter requestAiMovePresenter =
                new RequestAiMovePresenter(gameViewModel, uiScheduler);
        requestAiMoveController = new RequestAiMoveController(
                new RequestAiMoveInteractor(requestAiMovePresenter), gameViewModel, uiScheduler);
        return this;
    }

    public JFrame build() {
        return frame;
    }

    private static Runnable ifEnabled(BooleanSupplier enabled, Runnable effect) {
        return () -> {
            if (enabled.getAsBoolean()) {
                effect.run();
            }
        };
    }
}
```

{
  "content": "package game.start_new_game;\n\nimport game.GameState;\nimport game.GameViewModel;\nimport game.GameViewModelMapper;\nimport game.start_new_game.use_case.StartNewGameOutputBoundary;\nimport game.start_new_game.use_case.StartNewGameOutputData;\n\n/**\n * The Presenter for the Start New Game Use Case. Stashes the session data\n * (mode and AI strategy) in the shared bean, updates the render state, and\n * fires a property change so the view re-renders.\n */\npublic class StartNewGamePresenter implements StartNewGameOutputBoundary {\n\n    private final GameViewModel gameViewModel;\n\n    public StartNewGamePresenter(GameViewModel gameViewModel) {\n        this.gameViewModel = gameViewModel;\n    }\n\n    @Override\n    public void prepareSuccessView(StartNewGameOutputData outputData) {\n        final GameState state = gameViewModel.getState();\n        state.setCurrentGameState(outputData.gameState());\n        state.setMode(outputData.mode());\n        state.setAiStrategy(outputData.aiStrategy());\n        state.setBoard(GameViewModelMapper.toBoardViewModel(outputData.gameState()));\n        state.setStatus(GameViewModelMapper.toStatusViewModel(outputData.gameState()));\n        state.setError(null);\n        gameViewModel.firePropertyChanged();\n    }\n\n    @Override\n    public void prepareFailView(String error) {\n        final GameState state = gameViewModel.getState();\n        state.setError(error);\n        gameViewModel.firePropertyChanged();\n    }\n}",
  "filePath": "/Users/pgries/Projects/ca_examples/tictactoe/src/main/java/game/start_new_game/StartNewGamePresenter.java"
}

Builds the input data from\n * primitives (as the CAWithBuilder controllers do) and remembers the last\n * input so the view can request a restart with the same settings.\n */\npublic class StartNewGameController {\n\n    private final StartNewGameInputBoundary startNewGameUseCase;\n\n    private StartNewGameInputData lastInput;\n\n    public StartNewGameController(StartNewGameInputBoundary startNewGameUseCase) {\n        this.startNewGameUseCase = startNewGameUseCase;\n    }\n\n    public void execute(int boardSize, int winLength, GameMode mode,\n                        Optional<AiDifficulty> aiDifficulty) {\n        final StartNewGameInputData inputData = new StartNewGameInputData(\n                new GameConfig(boardSize, winLength), mode, aiDifficulty);\n        this.lastInput = inputData;\n\n        startNewGameUseCase.execute(inputData);\n    }\n\n    public void restart() {\n        startNewGameUseCase.execute(lastInput);\n    }\n}",

{
  "content": "package game.start_new_game;\n\nimport framework.ViewManagerModel;\nimport game.GameState;\nimport game.GameViewModel;\nimport game.GameViewModelMapper;\nimport game.start_new_game.use_case.StartNewGameOutputBoundary;\nimport game.start_new_game.use_case.StartNewGameOutputData;\n\n/**\n * The Presenter for the Start New Game Use Case. Stashes the session data\n * (mode and AI strategy) in the shared bean, updates the render state, and\n * fires a property change so the view re-renders. Navigation is\n * presenter-driven through the {@link ViewManagerModel}, as in\n * CAWithBuilder.\n */\npublic class StartNewGamePresenter implements StartNewGameOutputBoundary {\n\n    private final GameViewModel gameViewModel;\n    private final ViewManagerModel viewManagerModel;\n    private final String setupViewName;\n\n    public StartNewGamePresenter(\n            GameViewModel gameViewModel,\n            ViewManagerModel viewManagerModel,\n            String setupViewName) {\n        this.gameViewModel = gameViewModel;\n        this.viewManagerModel = viewManagerModel;\n        this.setupViewName = setupViewName;\n    }\n\n    @Override\n    public void prepareSuccessView(StartNewGameOutputData outputData) {\n        final GameState state = gameViewModel.getState();\n        state.setCurrentGameState(outputData.gameState());\n        state.setMode(outputData.mode());\n        state.setAiStrategy(outputData.aiStrategy());\n        state.setBoard(GameViewModelMapper.toBoardViewModel(outputData.gameState()));\n        state.setStatus(GameViewModelMapper.toStatusViewModel(outputData.gameState()));\n        state.setError(null);\n        gameViewModel.firePropertyChanged();\n\n        viewManagerModel.setState(gameViewModel.getViewName());\n        viewManagerModel.firePropertyChanged();\n    }\n\n    @Override\n    public void prepareFailView(String error) {\n        final GameState state = gameViewModel.getState();\n        state.setError(error);\n        gameViewModel.firePropertyChanged();\n    }\n\n    @Override\n    public void switchToSetupView() {\n        viewManagerModel.setState(setupViewName);\n        viewManagerModel.firePropertyChanged();\n    }\n}",
  "filePath": "/Users/pgries/Projects/ca_examples/tictactoe/src/main/java/game/start_new_game/StartNewGamePresenter.java"
}

The user asks to explain Delta #4 again: the firePropertyChanged(String) overload on framework/ViewModel.

From the comparison: CAWithBuilder's ViewModel has both `firePropertyChanged()` and `firePropertyChanged(String propertyName)`. The no-arg version fires a "state" property change. The overload lets a listener distinguish multiple kinds of changes by name. In CAWithBuilder, ChangePasswordPresenter fires "password" and ChangePasswordView.propertyChange distinguishes events by name.

Tictactoe's ViewModel only has the no-arg one, which fires "state". The ViewManager relies on "state" (evt.getPropertyName().equals("state")). MainFrame listens on GameViewModel and ignores the property name (just reads new value).

So why would it matter for tictactoe? Currently nothing needs the overload. In CAWithBuilder it's used because a single view listens to multiple kinds of changes (password errors vs username errors vs navigation). Tictactoe's MainFrame renders everything from one bean and doesn't need to distinguish event types. So Delta #4 is an API-completeness match, not a functional need.

Be concise.

</details>

In CAWithBuilder, `framework/ViewModel` has **two** fire methods:

```java
public void firePropertyChanged()                    // fires "state"
public void firePropertyChanged(String propertyName) // fires <custom name>
```

The no-arg version always fires the event under the property name `"state"` (that's what `ViewManager` listens for). The overload lets a presenter fire an event under a *different* name, so a view listening to multiple sources can tell them apart — CAWithBuilder uses it in `ChangePasswordPresenter` (fires `"password"`) and `ChangePasswordView.propertyChange` switches on `evt.getPropertyName()`.

Tictactoe's `ViewModel` only has the no-arg version. Nothing here needs the overload today — `MainFrame` renders from the single shared `GameState` bean and ignores event names, and the new `ViewManager` relies on `"state"`. So Delta #4 is purely an API-completeness match with the reference, not a functional gap.

Worth doing? It's 5 lines (plus the javadoc), but I'd say only if you want the two files to be drop-in comparable for teaching. Otherwise it's fine to leave.

Here's the analysis — grounded in the current code on `presenter-appbuilder`.

## 1. Dependency Rule / boundary violations

**a) Start New Game signals failure by exception, not through the boundary — the biggest one.**
`StartNewGameInteractor.execute` calls `gameStateFactory.newGame(...)`; `GameConfig`'s compact constructor throws `InvalidGameConfigException` (src/main/java/game/domain/GameConfig.java:7). Nothing catches it: the exception travels through the interactor → controller → and is caught by the **view** (`SetupPanel` imports `game.domain.exception.InvalidGameConfigException` and try/catches around `controller.execute`, SetupPanel.java:142-148). The other two interactors do it correctly (`MakeHumanMoveInteractor` catches `InvalidMoveException` → `prepareFailView`). Consequences:
- The use case's failure channel (`prepareFailView`) is **dead code in production** for StartNewGame.
- The UI layer depends on a *domain exception type* — an outward dependency that leaks domain internals to the view.

Fix: the interactor catches and calls `prepareFailView(e.getMessage())`; `SetupPanel` drops its try/catch.

**b) The presentation bean is a mini-god-object that crosses layers.** `game/GameState` holds render data (board/status), session data (mode, strategy, pendingAiBase), **and the whole domain aggregate**, and implements game policy: `isAiTurn()` (GameState.java:84) hardcodes `Mark.X.other()` instead of reusing the domain's `STARTING_MARK`. The name-collision with `game.domain.GameState` compounds it. Documented deviation, but worth re-examining.

**c) Use cases coupled through the shared bean.** The AI strategy is *created* by the StartNewGame use case, stashed in the session, and *consumed* by RequestAiMove — transported through `RequestAiMoveInputData`. And `MakeHumanMovePresenter` triggers another use case's controller directly via the `Runnable`. Neither exists in CAWithBuilder (presenters only navigate). The alternative — `RequestAiMoveInteractor` receiving `AiStrategyFactory` + difficulty in `InputData` — would make each use case self-contained.

**d) "framework" isn't generic.** `MainFrame`/`SetupPanel`/`StatusPanel` import capability controllers and game view-model types. Direction is legal (outer→inner), but the package is app-specific UI masquerading as infrastructure — CAWithBuilder puts views in capability packages. Documented deviation.

## 2. SOLID

- **S**: `GameState` bean (render + session + policy) and `MainFrame` (render + error dialog + win effects + theme) carry several responsibilities; `SetupPanel` is borderline (form + validation + effect toggles). Everything else is single-purpose.
- **O**: `AiStrategyFactory.create` is a `switch` on `AiDifficulty` — adding a difficulty edits the enum *and* the factory. Minor; an `EnumMap` would make it open/closed.
- **L**: clean — no violations found (`AiStrategy` implementations, sealed `GameStatus` hierarchy).
- **I**: boundaries are small; `switchToSetupView` on both boundaries is a pass-through, mirroring CAWithBuilder's `switchToLoginView`. OK.
- **D**: strong — presenters implement `OutputBoundary`, controllers depend on `InputBoundary`, `AppBuilder` composes. 

## 3. A real concurrency bug (stale-discard is unsound)

`RequestAiMoveController.execute()` sets the single `pendingAiBase` slot, then reads it **lazily inside the background lambda** (RequestAiMoveController.java:36). The presenter's staleness check compares `currentGameState` against that single shared slot. With two overlapping AI requests the check can pass for the **wrong** result:

1. AI computing slowly on game A (10×10 minimax is seconds).
2. User clicks Restart → new AI game, human moves quickly → request #2 sets `pendingAiBase = base2`.
3. Old task finishes, reads `pendingAiBase` (now `base2`), presents result₁ (computed from `base1`). Check: `currentGameState == base2 == pendingAiBase` → **not stale** → garbage move applied.
4. Task #2's result₂ then fails the check (`currentGameState` = result₁ ≠ `base2`) and is **discarded** — the wrong move wins.

Root cause: the base doesn't travel with the request; it lives in one mutable slot. Fix: capture the base eagerly on the EDT at `execute()` time and echo it through the boundary — e.g. `RequestAiMoveOutputData(updatedState, base)`, with the presenter comparing against `outputData.base()`.

## 4. Minor

- `AppBuilder.addMakeHumanMoveUseCase()` NPEs if called before `addRequestAiMoveUseCase()` (order-coupled wiring).
- `StartNewGameController.restart()` NPEs if called before any `execute()` (unreachable in the UI today).

**Suggested priority**: 1a (boundary violation), 3 (bug), 1b/1c (design), 2/4 (polish). Want me to fix any of these?

**Subject:** `fix: route start-new-game failures through the boundary and harden AI staleness`

**Body:**
```
Start New Game failed through an InvalidGameConfigException that the view
caught (framework importing a domain exception type); prepareFailView was
dead code. InputData now carries primitives and the interactor builds the
GameConfig, so invalid settings reach the presenter through the output
boundary like every other failure.

The AI staleness discard compared the session against a single
pendingAiBase slot read lazily in the background, so an overlapping AI
request (restart into a new AI game) could apply the old result and
discard the new one. The base now travels with the request: captured
eagerly on the UI thread and echoed through RequestAiMoveOutputData, and
the pendingAiBase slot is gone.

Also guard the fragile AppBuilder wiring order and restart() before the
first execute(). 105 tests pass, including three new ones.
```

I'd split it along its two real consumers — presentation and session — and delete its policy method.

**Recommended shape:**

```
GameViewModel (observable; holds both, fires once)
├── SessionState      // written by presenters, read/snapshotted by controllers
│   ├── currentGameState   (game.domain.GameState)
│   ├── mode               (GameMode)
│   └── aiStrategy         (Optional<AiStrategy>)
└── GameRenderState   // written by presenters, read by MainFrame
    ├── board   (BoardViewModel)
    ├── status  (StatusViewModel)
    └── error   (String)
```

- Controllers snapshot from `session`; `MainFrame` renders only from `render` — the view can no longer reach domain state, and the `game.GameState` / `game.domain.GameState` name collision dies.
- `GameViewModel` stays the single observable, so the "update state, fire once" presenter pattern and `MainFrame`'s single listener are untouched.
- **`isAiTurn()` policy leaves the bean entirely.** The "is it O's turn" check becomes controller-local logic using the domain constant — e.g. in `MakeHumanMoveController`: `!state.isGameOver() && state.currentTurn() == game.domain.GameState.STARTING_MARK.other()` (optionally a named domain helper `currentTurnIs(Mark)` if you want the expression reusable). Game rules no longer live in presentation state.

**Minimal alternative** (if you'd rather stay closer to CAWithBuilder's single shared bean): keep one bean but rename it `PresentationState` (kills the collision), drop `isAiTurn()` the same way, and leave session + render fields side by side. That fixes the policy and naming criticisms but not the mixed responsibilities.

**Trade-offs:**
- The split is ~2 new small classes and mechanical churn in the controller/presenter tests (they use `getState().setCurrentGameState(...)`/`setBoard(...)` etc. everywhere → `getSession()`/`getRender()`).
- It also updates the AGENTS.md wording, which currently documents "one shared presentation bean holding both render data and session data".
- If a future use case needs cross-cutting state (e.g. a high-score counter shared by several frames), the split makes the bean-per-frame story slightly less uniform.

My vote: the split — it's the one that actually removes the god object, and the collision fix is a teaching win.

40:   - `game/domain/` (shared domain model)
41:   - `app/`, `framework/`
42: - Build a `CommonUser`/`CommonUserFactory` style entity for domain models.
43: - Each use case gets a boundary set under its `use_case` package:
44:   `InputBoundary`, `InputData`, `Interactor`, `OutputBoundary`, `OutputData`.
45:   Interactors are `void` and receive the `OutputBoundary` in their
46:   constructor; the `OutputBoundary` is implemented by the capability's
47:   **Presenter**, which updates the shared `GameViewModel`/`GameState` bean and
48:   fires a PropertyChange; the `InputBoundary` is held by the capability's thin
49:   **Controller**, which builds the `InputData` from view primitives.
50: - View-state model: a `framework/ViewModel<T>` base plus a shared
51:   presentation bean (`GameState`) holding both render data (board/status) and
52:   session data (mode, AI strategy, stale-result base) that controllers and
53:   presenters share across use cases; one `MainFrame` renders from it.
54: - Navigation is presenter-driven: a `framework/ViewManager` +
55:   `ViewManagerModel` (`extends ViewModel<String>`) switches the card layout,
56:   presenters navigate by setting the view name (e.g. on success), and pure
57:   screen switches go through the boundaries as a second method
58:   (`switchToSetupView`, like CAWithBuilder's `switchToLoginView`). Card
59:   names come from `getViewName()` on the views.
60: - Wiring in `app/AppBuilder` (per-frame wiring methods); `Main` stays thin.
61: - Controllers/presenters may inject a `UiScheduler` (`framework`) to move
62:   work off the UI thread; stale background results are discarded by comparing
63:   the session state against the base the result was computed from.
64: - A one-frame presentation (`GameView`) or cross-cutting logic (win effects)
65:   that only serves the frame belongs inside the frame itself (e.g. a
66:   `Runnable` effect list on `MainFrame`), not in dedicated classes.

  "content": "package game;\n\nimport game.domain.GameMode;\n\n/**\n * Presentation-side game rules shared by the make-human-move controller\n * (ignore clicks while the AI is to move) and presenter (hand off to the\n * AI request after a human move).\n */\npublic final class GameSessionRules {\n\n    private GameSessionRules() {\n    }\n\n    public static boolean isAiTurn(SessionState session) {\n        return session.getMode() == GameMode.HUMAN_VS_AI\n            && session.getCurrentGameState() != null\n            && !session.getCurrentGameState().isGameOver()\n            && session.getCurrentGameState().currentTurn()\n                == game.domain.GameState.STARTING_MARK.other();\n    }\n}",

}

```
- Each use case gets a boundary set under its `use_case` package:
  `InputBoundary`, `InputData`, `Interactor`, `OutputBoundary`, `OutputData`.
  Interactors are `void` and receive the `OutputBoundary` in their
  constructor; the `OutputBoundary` is implemented by the capability's
  **Presenter**, which updates the shared `GameViewModel`/`GameState` bean and
  fires a PropertyChange; the `InputBoundary` is held by the capability's thin
  **Controller**, which builds the `InputData` from view primitives.
- View-state model: a `framework/ViewModel<T>` base plus a shared
  presentation bean (`GameState`) holding both render data (board/status) and
  session data (mode, AI strategy, stale-result base) that controllers and
  presenters share across use cases; one `MainFrame` renders from it.
```

New:
- Presenter updates the shared `GameViewModel` (its `SessionState`/`GameRenderState`) and fires a PropertyChange.
- View-state model: a `framework/ViewModel<T>` base plus a view model holding two separate states: a `SessionState` (current domain state, mode, AI strategy) shared by controllers and presenters, and a `GameRenderState` (board/status/error) that the frame renders from; presenters update both and fire one property change; one `MainFrame` renders from the render state. Presentation-side rules shared by several use cases (e.g. is the AI to move) live in a small static helper (`GameSessionRules`), not on the state beans.

Also the "stale background results" bullet already says "comparing the session state against the base the result was computed from" — still accurate.

This one is about *which use case knows what about the AI strategy*. Here's the concrete trace through the current code:

**The flow today:**

1. **Start New Game** creates the strategy it never uses:
   `StartNewGameInteractor.execute` runs `aiStrategyFactory.create(difficulty)` (src/main/java/game/start_new_game/use_case/StartNewGameInteractor.java:31) purely to hand it to the presenter, which stashes it in `SessionState.setAiStrategy(...)` (StartNewGamePresenter.java:37).
2. **Request AI Move** later fishes it back out: `RequestAiMoveController.execute` reads `session.getAiStrategy()` (RequestAiMoveController.java:33) and passes the object through `RequestAiMoveInputData` to its interactor.

So the strategy's journey is: interactor A → output data A → presenter A → **session bean** → controller B → input data B → interactor B.

**Why that's a coupling:**

- **Start New Game's output carries another use case's collaborator.** Its `OutputData` includes an `AiStrategy` — a *behavior object* that StartNewGame itself never invokes. The only reason it exists there is that RequestAiMove needs it later. If RequestAiMove didn't exist, StartNewGame would still create and ship it.
- **Hidden temporal contract.** RequestAiMove silently assumes StartNewGame ran first and stashed a strategy. The two use cases are welded together through shared mutable state; neither use case's boundary makes that relationship visible.
- **Behavior in input data.** `RequestAiMoveInputData` should say *what to do* (plain data); instead it carries the *doing* (a function object). That's the reverse of the Dependency Rule's intent at this layer — the interactor already knows the `AiStrategy` *interface*, so the boundary gains nothing by smuggling the implementation through the bean.
- **Isolation cost.** You can't exercise RequestAiMove in isolation — a test must first run StartNewGame (or hand-wire the session) to produce a strategy.

**The alternative I sketched** — make each use case self-contained:

- `SessionState` stores `AiDifficulty` (a plain domain value) instead of the strategy object.
- `RequestAiMoveInputData(difficulty, ...)` — data only.
- `RequestAiMoveInteractor(presenter, aiStrategyFactory)` creates its own strategy from the difficulty, exactly like StartNewGame does: `aiStrategyFactory.create(inputData.difficulty())`.

Then each use case owns its collaborators: StartNewGame creates the game and records *what was chosen*; RequestAiMove interprets that choice. The bean stops being the communication channel between use cases, and a change to how AI moves are requested touches only RequestAiMove.

**Cost:** the strategy is recreated on every AI request instead of once per game — negligible here (`Random` holds a `Random`, `Easy`/`Minimax` are cheap value objects, and the interactor runs in the background anyway).

Note this is distinct from finding #3 (the `MakeHumanMovePresenter` → `RequestAiMoveController` `Runnable`): #3 is *triggering* another use case, #2 is *feeding* it data through shared state. Both are "use cases no longer independent"; #2 is the one where the boundaries themselves leak.

Good timing — this is exactly the change that forces the persistence boundary to appear (the repo has no DAO yet, which AGENTS.md calls out as a teaching note). Here's what I'd do, in order:

## 1. Session must store `AiDifficulty`, not `AiStrategy` (prerequisite)

This is the blocker. `SessionState` currently holds an `AiStrategy` — a *behavior object* you cannot serialize. A saved game must remember "vs computer, EASY", which is a plain enum value. So before anything else:

- `SessionState.setAiStrategy(...)` → `setDifficulty(AiDifficulty)`
- `RequestAiMove` becomes self-contained (finding #2's alternative becomes *necessary*): its interactor takes `AiStrategyFactory`, its `InputData` carries the difficulty, and it creates its own strategy per request.
- `StartNewGameInteractor` stops creating the strategy; it just records the difficulty.

This is the change I'd argue for even without save/load — persistence just makes it unavoidable.

## 2. Two new capability packages (the structural change)

Following package-by-capability, one folder per use case, each with the full boundary set plus a **data-access boundary**:

```
game/save_game/
├── SaveGameController, SaveGamePresenter
└── use_case/
    ├── SaveGameInputBoundary, SaveGameInputData
    ├── SaveGameInteractor
    ├── SaveGameOutputBoundary, SaveGameOutputData
    └── SaveGameDataAccess          // the new boundary type
game/load_game/
├── LoadGameController, LoadGamePresenter
└── use_case/
    ├── LoadGameInputBoundary, LoadGameInputData
    ├── LoadGameInteractor
    ├── LoadGameOutputBoundary, LoadGameOutputData
    └── LoadGameDataAccess
```

This mirrors CAWithBuilder exactly: each use case declares the narrow interface it needs (ISP), and the concrete DAO implements both. The interactor is `void`, takes the `OutputBoundary` + the data access in its constructor, and errors (no saved game, corrupt file) go through `prepareFailView` like every other failure.

## 3. The implementation lives in the outer layer

`framework/storage/FileGameStore implements SaveGameDataAccess, LoadGameDataAccess` — `framework` is already the outer ring (it holds `ui/`), so persistence joins it there rather than creating a CAWithBuilder-style top-level `data_access` package (which would break this repo's "layers live inside capabilities" convention). It owns the file format entirely — serializing the domain aggregate to/from whatever text format you choose (this repo has zero external deps, so a small hand-rolled format or `Properties` fits). The domain model stays persistence-ignorant: nothing in `game/domain` changes.

## 4. Wiring and navigation

- `AppBuilder` gains `addSaveGameUseCase()` / `addLoadGameUseCase()`, constructs the single `FileGameStore`, and injects it into both interactors.
- A "Save" button on the game screen (in `StatusPanel`, its `Runnable`-list pattern) and a "Resume" button on the setup screen. Loading is presenter-driven navigation exactly like start-new-game: `LoadGamePresenter` restores session (state + mode + difficulty) and render halves, then navigates to the game view on success.
- `StartNewGamePresenter` already knows how to populate both halves — `LoadGamePresenter` will look almost identical, which is a nice symmetry to teach.

One caution: the AI strategy creation currently happens *at game start* so the session holds one strategy for the whole game. With the change in #1, that rationale disappears, and the per-request creation cost is negligible.

Builds a fresh game\n * through the injected {@link GameStateFactory} — as CAWithBuilder's\n * interactors receive their factories in the constructor. It records the\n * chosen AI difficulty but creates no strategy; the request-AI-move use\n * case builds its own strategy from the difficulty for each move.\n */\npublic final class StartNewGameInteractor implements StartNewGameInputBoundary {\n\n    private final StartNewGameOutputBoundary presenter;\n    private final GameStateFactory gameStateFactory;\n\n    public StartNewGameInteractor(\n            StartNewGameOutputBoundary presenter,\n            GameStateFactory gameStateFactory) {\n        this.presenter = presenter;\n        this.gameStateFactory = gameStateFactory;\n    }\n\n    @Override\n    public void execute(StartNewGameInputData inputData) {\n        try {\n            final GameConfig config = new GameConfig(inputData.boardSize(), inputData.winLength());\n            presenter.prepareSuccessView(new StartNewGameOutputData(\n                    gameStateFactory.newGame(config),\n                    inputData.mode(),\n                    inputData.aiDifficulty()));\n        } catch (InvalidGameConfigException e) {\n            presenter.prepareFailView(e.getMessage());\n        }\n    }",
  "oldString": "import game.ai.AiStrategy;\nimport game.ai.AiStrategyFactory;\nimport game.domain.GameConfig;\nimport game.domain.GameStateFactory;\nimport game.domain.exception.InvalidGameConfigException;\nimport java.util.Optional;\n\n/**\n * The Interactor for the Start New Game Use Case. Builds a fresh game\n * through the injected {@link GameStateFactory} and, for AI games, the AI\n * strategy through the injected {@link AiStrategyFactory} — as\n * CAWithBuilder's interactors receive their factories in the constructor.\n */\npublic final class StartNewGameInteractor implements StartNewGameInputBoundary {\n\n    private final StartNewGameOutputBoundary presenter;\n    private final GameStateFactory gameStateFactory;\n    private final AiStrategyFactory aiStrategyFactory;\n\n    public StartNewGameInteractor(\n            StartNewGameOutputBoundary presenter,\n            GameStateFactory gameStateFactory,\n            AiStrategyFactory aiStrategyFactory) {\n        this.presenter = presenter;\n        this.gameStateFactory = gameStateFactory;\n        this.aiStrategyFactory = aiStrategyFactory;\n    }\n\n    @Override\n    public void execute(StartNewGameInputData inputData) {\n        final Optional<AiStrategy> aiStrategy = inputData.aiDifficulty()\n                .map(aiStrategyFactory::create);\n        try {\n            final GameConfig config = new GameConfig(inputData.boardSize(), inputData.winLength());\n            presenter.prepareSuccessView(new StartNewGameOutputData(\n                    gameStateFactory.newGame(config),\n                    inputData.mode(),\n                    aiStrategy));\n        } catch (InvalidGameConfigException e) {\n            presenter.prepareFailView(e.getMessage());\n        }\n    }"

  "content": "package game.request_ai_move.use_case;\n\nimport game.ai.AiStrategy;\nimport game.ai.AiStrategyFactory;\nimport game.domain.GameState;\nimport game.domain.Position;\nimport game.domain.exception.InvalidMoveException;\n\n/**\n * The Interactor for the Request AI Move Use Case. Builds the AI strategy\n * from the requested difficulty through the injected {@link AiStrategyFactory}\n * and applies the move to the snapshot it is given.\n */\npublic final class RequestAiMoveInteractor implements RequestAiMoveInputBoundary {\n\n    private final RequestAiMoveOutputBoundary presenter;\n    private final AiStrategyFactory aiStrategyFactory;\n\n    public RequestAiMoveInteractor(\n            RequestAiMoveOutputBoundary presenter,\n            AiStrategyFactory aiStrategyFactory) {\n        this.presenter = presenter;\n        this.aiStrategyFactory = aiStrategyFactory;\n    }\n\n    @Override\n    public void execute(RequestAiMoveInputData inputData) {\n        if (inputData.state().isGameOver()) {\n            presenter.prepareFailView(\"cannot request an AI move after the game is over\");\n            return;\n        }\n\n        final AiStrategy strategy = aiStrategyFactory.create(inputData.difficulty());\n        Position move = strategy\n            .selectMove(inputData.state().board(), inputData.state().config(), inputData.state().currentTurn());\n        try {\n            GameState updated = inputData.state().applyMove(move);\n            presenter.prepareSuccessView(new RequestAiMoveOutputData(updated, inputData.state()));\n        } catch (InvalidMoveException e) {\n            presenter.prepareFailView(e.getMessage());\n        }\n    }\n}",
  "filePath": "/Users/pgries/Projects/ca_examples/tictactoe/src/main/java/game/request_ai_move/use_case/RequestAiMoveInteractor.java"
}

**Subject:** `refactor: store AI difficulty in the session instead of the strategy`

**Body:**
```
The session bean carried an AiStrategy object that Start New Game
created and Request AI Move consumed, coupling the two use cases through
shared state and making the session impossible to serialize (a blocker
for the planned save/load).

The session now records the chosen AiDifficulty (a plain domain value);
Start New Game's output carries it through, and Request AI Move builds
its own strategy per move from its injected AiStrategyFactory, so each
use case owns its collaborators. The interactor test uses the real
factory (the class is final, so Mockito cannot mock it) and asserts
robust board properties instead of a specific move.
```

@Override
public boolean equals(Object other) {
    if (this == other) {
        return true;
    }
    if (!(other instanceof Board board)) {
        return false;
    }
    return size == board.size && Arrays.deepEquals(cells, board.cells);
}

@Override
public int hashCode() {
    int result = Objects.hash(size);
    result = 31 * result + Arrays.deepHashCode(cells);
    return result;
}

Board is a pure data class but compared by reference, so two
equal-content boards were unequal and game.domain.GameState (a record
containing Board) was not a true value type. This blocked save/load
round-trip tests (loaded.equals(saved)) and made the AI staleness check
reference-based. Add equals/hashCode over size and the cell grid, cover
them in BoardTest, and strengthen the request-AI-move interactor test
back to a whole-state equality assertion (the exact state produced by
the strategy's chosen move) now that value equality makes it possible.
```

public void execute(LoadGameInputData inputData) {
    try {
        Optional<SavedGame> saved = loadGameDataAccess.load();
        if (saved.isEmpty()) {
            presenter.prepareFailView("no saved game found");
        } else {
            presenter.prepareSuccessView(new LoadGameOutputData(saved.get()));
        }
    } catch (IOException e) {
        presenter.prepareFailView("could not load the saved game: " + e.getMessage());
    }
}

```java
public final class FileGameStore implements SaveGameDataAccess, LoadGameDataAccess {
    private final Path file;
    public FileGameStore(Path file) { this.file = file; }
    @Override public void save(SavedGame savedGame) throws IOException {
        if (file.getParent() != null) Files.createDirectories(file.getParent());
        Files.write(file, encode(savedGame));
    }
    @Override public Optional<SavedGame> load() throws IOException {
        if (!Files.exists(file)) return Optional.empty();
        List<String> lines = Files.readAllLines(file);
        try {
            return Optional.of(decode(lines));
        } catch (RuntimeException e) {
            throw new IOException("corrupt saved game: " + e.getMessage(), e);
        }
    }
    private List<String> encode(SavedGame saved) { ... }
    private SavedGame decode(List<String> lines) { ... }
}
```

Snapshots the current session\n * from the shared view model.\n */\npublic class SaveGameController {\n\n    private final SaveGameInputBoundary saveGameUseCase;\n    private final GameViewModel gameViewModel;\n\n    public SaveGameController(\n            SaveGameInputBoundary saveGameUseCase,\n            GameViewModel gameViewModel) {\n        this.saveGameUseCase = saveGameUseCase;\n        this.gameViewModel = gameViewModel;\n    }\n\n    public void execute() {\n        final SessionState session = gameViewModel.getSession();\n        if (session.getCurrentGameState() == null) {\n            throw new IllegalStateException(\"no game in progress to save\");\n        }\n        saveGameUseCase.execute(new SaveGameInputData(\n                session.getCurrentGameState(), session.getMode(), session.getDifficulty()));\n    }\n}",

Confirms the save through the\n * frame's transient message channel; failures go the same way.\n */\npublic class SaveGamePresenter implements SaveGameOutputBoundary {\n\n    private final GameViewModel gameViewModel;\n\n    public SaveGamePresenter(GameViewModel gameViewModel) {\n        this.gameViewModel = gameViewModel;\n    }\n\n    @Override\n    public void prepareSuccessView(SaveGameOutputData outputData) {\n        gameViewModel.getState().setMessage(\"Game saved\");\n        gameViewModel.firePropertyChanged();\n    }\n\n    @Override\n    public void prepareFailView(String error) {\n        gameViewModel.getState().setMessage(error);\n        gameViewModel.firePropertyChanged();\n    }\n}",

{
  "content": "package game.load_game.use_case;\n\nimport java.io.IOException;\nimport java.util.Optional;\n\n/**\n * The Interactor for the Load Game Use Case. Loads the saved session through\n * the persistence boundary and routes \"no saved game\" and persistence\n * failures through the output boundary, never to the view.\n */\npublic final class LoadGameInteractor implements LoadGameInputBoundary {\n\n    private final LoadGameOutputBoundary presenter;\n    private final LoadGameDataAccess loadGameDataAccess;\n\n    public LoadGameInteractor(\n            LoadGameOutputBoundary presenter,\n            LoadGameDataAccess loadGameDataAccess) {\n        this.presenter = presenter;\n        this.loadGameDataAccess = loadGameDataAccess;\n    }\n\n    @Override\n    public void execute(LoadGameInputData inputData) {\n        try {\n            Optional<game.domain.SavedGame> savedGame = loadGameDataAccess.load();\n            if (savedGame.isEmpty()) {\n                presenter.prepareFailView(\"no saved game found\");\n            } else {\n                presenter.prepareSuccessView(new LoadGameOutputData(savedGame.get()));\n            }\n        } catch (IOException e) {\n            presenter.prepareFailView(\"could not load the saved game: \" + e.getMessage());\n        }\n    }\n}",
  "filePath": "/Users/pgries/Projects/ca_examples/tictactoe/src/main/java/game/load_game/use_case/LoadGameInteractor.java"
}

LoadGamePresenterTest {\n\n    private GameViewModel gameViewModel;\n    private ViewManagerModel viewManagerModel;\n    private LoadGamePresenter presenter;\n    private GameRenderState lastFiredState;\n    private int fireCount;\n\n    @BeforeEach\n    void setUp() {\n        gameViewModel = new GameViewModel();\n        viewManagerModel = new ViewManagerModel();\n        PropertyChangeListener listener = evt -> {\n            lastFiredState = (GameRenderState) evt.getNewValue();\n            fireCount++;\n        };\n        gameViewModel.addPropertyChangeListener(listener);\n        presenter = new LoadGamePresenter(gameViewModel, viewManagerModel);\n    }\n\n    @Test\n    void prepareSuccessView_RestoresSessionAndRenderAndNavigates() {\n        SavedGame savedGame = new SavedGame(\n                GameFixtures.wonByX(), GameMode.HUMAN_VS_AI, Optional.of(AiDifficulty.MEDIUM));\n\n        presenter.prepareSuccessView(new LoadGameOutputData(savedGame));\n\n        assertThat(gameViewModel.getSession().getCurrentGameState()).isEqualTo(savedGame.gameState());\n        assertThat(gameViewModel.getSession().getMode()).isEqualTo(GameMode.HUMAN_VS_AI);\n        assertThat(gameViewModel.getSession().getDifficulty()).contains(AiDifficulty.MEDIUM);\n        GameRenderState render = gameViewModel.getState();\n        assertThat(render.getBoard().cells()).hasSize(9);\n        assertThat(render.getBoard().cells().get(0).symbol()).isEqualTo(CellSymbol.X);\n        assertThat(render.getStatus().message()).isEqualTo(\"X wins!\");\n        assertThat(render.getMessage()).isNull();\n        assertThat(fireCount).isEqualTo(1);\n        assertThat(lastFiredState).isSameAs(render);\n        assertThat(viewManagerModel.getState()).isEqualTo(\"game\");\n    }\n\n    @Test\n    void prepareFailView_SetsMessageAndDoesNotNavigate() {\n        presenter.prepareFailView(\"no saved game found\");\n\n        assertThat(gameViewModel.getState().getMessage()).isEqualTo(\"no saved game found\");\n        assertThat(fireCount).isEqualTo(1);\n        assertThat(viewManagerModel.getState()).isEmpty();\n    }\n}",

Four real bugs, all in the store:

1. **`rebuildState` breaks on finished games**: `applyMove` throws `InvalidMoveException("cannot move after the game is over")` once a Win/Draw occurs mid-replay — the drawn game's final move completes the draw, and then... wait, in drawn game the last applyMove produces the Draw status; there are no more moves. The error is "cannot move after the game is over" — because in the drawn board the last move is applied and produces Draw; no further moves. Hmm — but for the won game: wonByX has 5 moves, X wins on move 5, no more moves. Where does "cannot move after the game is over" come from? For `drawn()`: 9 moves, last produces Draw — that's the 9th, no more moves. Hmm wait — the error happens in `load_DrawnGame_RecomputesDrawStatus`. Let me think: `drawn()` board has 9 cells. Replaying: moves 1..8 fine, move 9 completes the board → Draw. No move 10. So why?

Oh! The bug: my replay loops over ALL cells of the *parsed* board — fine. But `wonByX` case: the failure shows loaded = InProgress with currentTurn=O and board equal?? The board printed as `Board@c8b6cfe3` — the actual board is not shown nicely. Loaded state: status=InProgress, currentTurn=O. The saved was Win.

The issue: replay order. `wonByXBoard`-equivalent: moves X(0,0), O(1,0), X(0,1), O(1,1), X(0,2). Replaying in row-major order over the *parsed board*: row 0: (0,0) X, (0,1) X, (0,2) X — these three X moves in a row! After X(0,0) and X(0,1), the third move X(0,2) completes the top row → applyMove produces a Win AFTER only 3 moves... wait no, applyMove computes status from the *updated board*, so after X(0,0),X(0,1),X(0,2) it's a Win — then O(1,0) → throws "cannot move after the game is over".

Yes! The replay must apply moves in *chronological* order, but the file only stores the final board. The winning line is already complete; applying the remaining O moves after a win throws.

The real problem: **`applyMove` can't be used to replay a finished game** because it throws once the game is over. And even for non-finished games, replaying in row-major order could complete a line mid-replay (for a won game the line exists already — unavoidable).

Fix options:
- A: Rebuild board cell-by-cell without status checks: build GameState via `GameState.newGame(config)` then reconstruct the board using `Board.placeMark` directly in row-major order, then wrap: `new GameState(board, turn, config, WinChecker.evaluate(board, config))`. placeMark doesn't check game-over. Turn = derived from move count parity.

That's clean: the store reconstructs the Board directly (placing marks), computes turn from count, and status via WinChecker. No applyMove. But wait — Board.placeMark requires empty cells; the parsed board cells are placed once each. Good.

Turn derivation: count of placed marks. X starts → even count → X's turn; odd → O. `count % 2 == 0 ? Mark.X : Mark.O`.

2. **InvalidGameConfigException escapes as IllegalArgumentException**: `parseSavedGame` catches `IllegalArgumentException | IllegalStateException` — but `GameConfig` throws `InvalidGameConfigException`. What does that extend? Let me check — it threw out of load() as InvalidGameConfigException, so it's not an IllegalArgumentException. Check the exception hierarchy. The test wants IOException with message "boardSize must be at least 2". I could catch `RuntimeException` in load() — but that's broad; or make InvalidGameConfigException extend IllegalArgumentException. Hmm — domain fix vs store fix. Actually the cleanest: in `parseSavedGame`, the config construction is a parse-time concern; the store should catch the config exception explicitly and rethrow as IllegalArgumentException("boardSize must be at least 2: 1")... but that message is the domain's. Alternatively catch RuntimeException in load(). Let me check what InvalidGameConfigException extends first.

3. **Save with Win status is impossible to round-trip via replay** — fixed by option A.

Also note: after fix A, `currentTurn` for wonByX (5 moves) = O — matches saved (currentTurn=O, status Win). Round-trip equality holds since I recompute status from board via WinChecker = Win with the same winning line? WinChecker.evaluate scans LineGenerator.allLines in order — top row first for a 3x3. Saved game's winningLine: `findWinningLineThrough` — for wonByX, X's last move (0,2) — winning line = top row. WinChecker.evaluate finds the first winning line in generation order — top row would also be first (diagonal/column after rows). Should match. Draw: full board → Draw. Good.

4. Also the `load_HandWrittenFile_DerivesTurnAndStatus` test: board=X__/_O_/___ → 2 marks → turn X, InProgress. Fine with fix A.

Let me check InvalidGameConfigException's superclass.

Framework Independence\n\n###  10\\.1 Switching from Express to Fastify\n\nYou can swap the framework without changing the domain or use cases at all.\n\n```\n\n...\n\nWhat is the Dependency Rule in Clean Architecture?\n\n**A1.** The Dependency Rule states that **source code dependencies must always point inward (toward higher-level policies)** . Outer layers (frameworks, DB) depending on inner layers (Use Cases, Entities) is allowed, but inner layers directly depending on outer layers is forbidden. This ensures the domain is unaffected by framework or database changes. Q2. What is the difference between Port and Adapter in Hexagonal Architecture?\n\n**A2.** A **Port** is an **interface defined by the domain** (application core). It defines the contract for how the domain interacts with the outside world. An **Adapter** is **external technology that implements a Port** . For example, `OrderRepository` (Port) is implemented by `PostgresOrderRepository` (Adapter). Ports live in the domain layer; Adapters live in the infrastructure layer. Q3. What do Clean Architecture, Hexagonal Architecture, and Onion Architecture have in common?\n\n**A3.\n** All three architectures share these goals: (1) **Domain at the center** , (2) **Dependencies point inward (toward the domain) only** , (3) **Domain isolated from external tech (DB, frameworks)** , (4) **Apply Dependency Inversion Principle** . The differences are mainly in terminology (layer names) and detailed layer distinctions. Q4. When should you NOT use Clean Architecture?\n\n**A4.** Clean Architecture has overhead, so it is unnecessary for (1) **simple CRUD apps** (little to no business logic), (2) **prototypes/MVPs** (goal is fast validation), (3) **short-term projects** (no maintenance needed), (4) **solo small projects** (no need for team boundaries). In these cases, a traditional 3-layer architecture is more efficient. Q5. Why is framework independence important? Do people actually swap frameworks in practice?\n\n**A5.** The true value of framework independence lies in **testability** and **domain focus** rather than swapping itself.\nWhen the domain does not depend on the framework: (1) pure unit tests become possible, (2) domain logic becomes clearer, (3) framework upgrades become easier. In practice, transitions like Express to Fastify or REST to GraphQL happen frequently, and being able to leave domain code untouched is a significant advantage.\n\n* * *\n\n##  14\\. 443:                 return 0f;
444:             }
445:             if (t < FADE_MS) {
446:                 return t / (float) FADE_MS;
447:             }
448:             if (t > FADE_MS + HOLD_MS) {
449:                 return (CYCLE_MS - t) / (float) FADE_MS;
450:             }
451:             return 1f;
452:         }
453:     }

SetupPanel design (CAWithBuilder binding):
- Constructor takes SetupViewModel; adds itself as PropertyChangeListener.
- Spinner ChangeListeners write boardSize/winLength into state.
- Radio buttons: ItemListener sets mode in state and enables difficultyBox.
- difficultyBox: ItemListener sets difficulty in state.
- Win-effect checkboxes: ItemListener sets toggles in state.
- Night mode checkbox: stays Theme-only.
- propertyChange: reads state.message, shows dialog, clears it.
- Start button: reads state → controller.execute(...).
- No more isConfettiEffectEnabled() etc. — AppBuilder reads from setupViewModel.
- keep clampWinLengthToBoardSize (view-side constraint).

Note difficulty state semantics: difficulty is Optional in state; the combo always has a selected item. Set difficulty from combo selection when mode is HUMAN_VS_AI. When mode is TWO_PLAYER → Optional.empty(). Write both radio and difficulty listeners to keep consistent.

30: ## Architecture
31: 
32: - **Clean Architecture**, package-by-capability.
33: - Structure: capability folder contains its `use_case` subpackage; layers live
34:   inside capabilities rather than top-level layers.
35: - Example layout:
36:   - `game/` (shared presentation bean and view-model)

41:   - `game/load_game/use_case` (persistence boundary: `LoadGameDataAccess`)
42:   - `game/domain/` (shared domain model, incl. `SavedGame` snapshot)
43:   - `app/`, `framework/`
44: - Build a `CommonUser`/`CommonUserFactory` style entity for domain models.
45: - Each use case gets a boundary set under its `use_case` package:
46:   `InputBoundary`, `InputData`, `Interactor`, `OutputBoundary`, `OutputData`.
47:   Interactors are `void` and receive the `OutputBoundary` in their
48:   constructor; the `OutputBoundary` is implemented by the capability's
49:   **Presenter**, which updates the shared `GameViewModel` state and
50:   fires a PropertyChange; the `InputBoundary` is held by the capability's thin
51:   **Controller**, which builds the `InputData` from view primitives.

56:   from.
57:   Presenters update both and fire one property change; one `MainFrame`
58:   renders from it. Presentation-side rules shared by several use cases (e.g.
59:   "is the AI to move?") live in a small static helper (`GameSessionRules`),
60:   not on the state beans, which stay dumb.
61: - Navigation is presenter-driven: a `framework/ViewManager` +
62:   `ViewManagerModel` (`extends ViewModel<String>`) switches the card layout,
63:   presenters navigate by setting the view name (e.g. on success), and pure
64:   screen switches go through the boundaries as a second method
65:   (`switchToSetupView`, like CAWithBuilder's `switchToLoginView`). Card
66:   names come from `getViewName()` on the views.
67: - Wiring in `app/AppBuilder` (per-frame wiring methods); `Main` stays thin.
68: - Controllers/presenters may inject a `UiScheduler` (`framework`) to move
69:   work off the UI thread; stale background results are discarded by comparing
70:   the session state against the base the result was computed from.

Design: A registry pattern:

```java
public final class AiStrategyFactory {

    private final Map<AiDifficulty, Supplier<AiStrategy>> strategies = new EnumMap<>(AiDifficulty.class);

    public AiStrategyFactory() {
        register(AiDifficulty.EASY, () -> new RandomAiStrategy(new Random()));
        register(AiDifficulty.MEDIUM, EasyAiStrategy::new);
        register(AiDifficulty.DIFFICULT, MinimaxAiStrategy::new);
    }

    public void register(AiDifficulty difficulty, Supplier<AiStrategy> strategySupplier) {
        strategies.put(difficulty, strategySupplier);
    }

    public AiStrategy create(AiDifficulty difficulty) {
        Supplier<AiStrategy> supplier = strategies.get(difficulty);
        if (supplier == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("no AI strategy registered for " + difficulty);
        }
        return supplier.get();
    }
}
```

This removes the switch, makes it extensible (register custom strategies in tests/AppBuilder), and keeps default behavior. Tests can now verify registration behavior and override. This is the "configurable/registered" approach mentioned.

Design details for CommonAiStrategyFactory:

```java
package game.ai;

import game.domain.AiDifficulty;
import java.util.EnumMap;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Random;
import java.util.function.Supplier;

public final class CommonAiStrategyFactory implements AiStrategyFactory {

    private final Map<AiDifficulty, Supplier<AiStrategy>> strategies =
            new EnumMap<>(AiDifficulty.class);

    public CommonAiStrategyFactory() {
        register(AiDifficulty.EASY, () -> new RandomAiStrategy(new Random()));
        register(AiDifficulty.MEDIUM, EasyAiStrategy::new);
        register(AiDifficulty.DIFFICULT, MinimaxAiStrategy::new);
    }

    public void register(AiDifficulty difficulty, Supplier<AiStrategy> strategy) {
        strategies.put(difficulty, strategy);
    }

    @Override
    public AiStrategy create(AiDifficulty difficulty) {
        Supplier<AiStrategy> strategy = strategies.get(difficulty);
        if (strategy == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("no AI strategy registered for " + difficulty);
        }
        return strategy.get();
    }
}
```

The question is how to split this into 2-3 capabilities.

Let me think about what natural groupings exist:

1. **Domain** (`game/domain/` + `game/ai/`): The domain model (GameState, Board, etc.) and the AI strategies. These could form a "game engine" capability — the core game logic that doesn't depend on the UI at all.

2. **Setup** (`game/setup/` + maybe `game/start_new_game/`): The setup screen + starting a new game. These are related — you configure a game, then start it. Could be a "game setup" capability.

3. **Play** (`game/game_view/` + `game/make_human_move/` + `game/request_ai_move/`): The actual gameplay — the game screen, human moves, AI moves.

4. **Persistence** (`game/save_game/` + `game/load_game/`): Save and load — could be a "persistence" capability, though we already moved the DAO implementation to top-level `data_access/`.

Let me think about how CAWithBuilder would do this. CAWithBuilder has:
- `account/` (signup + change_password)
- `authentication/` (login)
- `user/` (domain)

- `game/` → domain + engine (domain model, AI) — keep as `game/` or rename
- `game_setup/` or `setup/` → setup screen + start_new_game + the shared session? Hmm

public class MakeHumanMoveController {
    private final MakeHumanMoveInputBoundary makeHumanMoveUseCase;
    private final GameSessionDataAccess session;

    execute(int row, int column) {
        GameState state = session.getCurrentGameState();
        if (state == null || state.isGameOver() || GameSessionRules.isAiTurn(session.getMode(), state)) {
            return;
        }
        makeHumanMoveUseCase.execute(new MakeHumanMoveInputData(new Position(row, column)));
    }
}

9. **MakeHumanMoveInteractor**:
```java
public final class MakeHumanMoveInteractor implements MakeHumanMoveInputBoundary {
    private final MakeHumanMoveOutputBoundary presenter;
    private final GameSessionDataAccess session;

    execute(MakeHumanMoveInputData inputData) {
        GameState current = session.getCurrentGameState();
        if (current == null) {
            return;
        }
        try {
            GameState updated = current.applyMove(inputData.position());
            session.setCurrentGameState(updated);
            boolean aiToMoveNext = GameSessionRules.isAiTurn(session.getMode(), updated);
            presenter.prepareSuccessView(new MakeHumanMoveOutputData(updated, aiToMoveNext));
        } catch (InvalidMoveException e) {
            presenter.prepareFailView(e.getMessage());
        }
    }
}
```

package game;

import game.domain.AiDifficulty;
import game.domain.GameMode;
import game.domain.GameState;
import java.util.Optional;

/**
 * The application-layer session: the game in progress plus its settings,
 * shared by the use cases that operate on the current game. Implemented
 * in data_access (InMemoryGameSession), mirroring CAWithBuilder's
 * InMemoryUserDataAccessObject.
 */
public interface GameSessionDataAccess {

    GameState getCurrentGameState();

    GameMode getMode();

    Optional<AiDifficulty> getAiDifficulty();

    void setCurrentGame(GameState state, GameMode mode, Optional<AiDifficulty> difficulty);

    void setCurrentGameState(GameState state);
}

```java
package data_access;

import game.GameSessionDataAccess;
import game.domain.AiDifficulty;
import game.domain.GameMode;
import game.domain.GameState;
import java.util.Optional;

public final class InMemoryGameSession implements GameSessionDataAccess {

    private GameState currentGameState;
    private GameMode mode;
    private Optional<AiDifficulty> difficulty = Optional.empty();

    @Override public GameState getCurrentGameState() { return currentGameState; }
    @Override public GameMode getMode() { return mode; }
    @Override public Optional<AiDifficulty> getAiDifficulty() { return difficulty; }
    @Override public void setCurrentGame(GameState state, GameMode mode, Optional<AiDifficulty> difficulty) {
        this.currentGameState = state;
        this.mode = mode;
        this.difficulty = difficulty;
    }
    @Override public void setCurrentGameState(GameState state) { this.currentGameState = state; }
}
```

  "content": "package data_access;\n\nimport game.GameSessionDataAccess;\nimport game.domain.AiDifficulty;\nimport game.domain.GameMode;\nimport game.domain.GameState;\nimport java.util.Optional;\n\n/**\n * The in-memory {@link GameSessionDataAccess}: holds the current game state\n * and its settings for the lifetime of the session, like CAWithBuilder's\n * {@code InMemoryUserDataAccessObject}.\n */\npublic final class InMemoryGameSession implements GameSessionDataAccess {\n\n    private GameState currentGameState;\n    private GameMode mode;\n    private Optional<AiDifficulty> difficulty = Optional.empty();\n\n    @Override\n    public GameState getCurrentGameState() {\n        return currentGameState;\n    }\n\n    @Override\n    public GameMode getMode() {\n        return mode;\n    }\n\n    @Override\n    public Optional<AiDifficulty> getAiDifficulty() {\n        return difficulty;\n    }\n\n    @Override\n    public void setCurrentGame(GameState state, GameMode mode, Optional<AiDifficulty> difficulty) {\n        this.currentGameState = state;\n        this.mode = mode;\n        this.difficulty = difficulty;\n    }\n\n    @Override\n    public void setCurrentGameState(GameState state) {\n        this.currentGameState = state;\n    }\n}"
}

  "content": "package game.start_new_game.use_case;\n\nimport game.GameSessionDataAccess;\nimport game.domain.GameConfig;\nimport game.domain.GameState;\nimport game.domain.GameStateFactory;\nimport game.domain.exception.InvalidGameConfigException;\n\n/**\n * The Interactor for the Start New Game Use Case. Builds a fresh game\n * through the injected {@link GameStateFactory} — as CAWithBuilder's\n * interactors receive their factories in the constructor — and writes the\n * new session (state plus settings) to the application-layer session. It\n * records the chosen AI difficulty but creates no strategy; the\n * request-AI-move use case builds its own strategy from the difficulty for\n * each move.\n */\npublic final class StartNewGameInteractor implements StartNewGameInputBoundary {\n\n    private final StartNewGameOutputBoundary presenter;\n    private final GameStateFactory gameStateFactory;\n    private final GameSessionDataAccess session;\n\n    public StartNewGameInteractor(\n            StartNewGameOutputBoundary presenter,\n            GameStateFactory gameStateFactory,\n            GameSessionDataAccess session) {\n        this.presenter = presenter;\n        this.gameStateFactory = gameStateFactory;\n        this.session = session;\n    }\n\n    @Override\n    public void execute(StartNewGameInputData inputData) {\n        try {\n            final GameConfig config = new GameConfig(inputData.boardSize(), inputData.winLength());\n            final GameState gameState = gameStateFactory.newGame(config);\n            session.setCurrentGame(gameState, inputData.mode(), inputData.aiDifficulty());\n            presenter.prepareSuccessView(new StartNewGameOutputData(gameState));\n        } catch (InvalidGameConfigException e) {\n            presenter.prepareFailView(e.getMessage());\n        }\n    }\n\n    @Override\n    public void switchToSetupView() {\n        presenter.switchToSetupView();\n    }\n}",

  "content": "package game.start_new_game;\n\nimport framework.ViewManagerModel;\nimport game.GameRenderState;\nimport game.GameViewModel;\nimport game.GameViewModelMapper;\nimport game.setup.SetupViewModel;\nimport game.start_new_game.use_case.StartNewGameOutputBoundary;\nimport game.start_new_game.use_case.StartNewGameOutputData;\n\n/**\n * The Presenter for the Start New Game Use Case. Renders the fresh game\n * state from the output data and fires a property change so the game view\n * re-renders. Failures go to the setup view model, whose view shows them.\n * Navigation is presenter-driven through the {@link ViewManagerModel}, as in\n * CAWithBuilder.\n */\npublic class StartNewGamePresenter implements StartNewGameOutputBoundary {\n\n    private final GameViewModel gameViewModel;\n    private final SetupViewModel setupViewModel;\n    private final ViewManagerModel viewManagerModel;\n\n    public StartNewGamePresenter(\n            GameViewModel gameViewModel,\n            SetupViewModel setupViewModel,\n            ViewManagerModel viewManagerModel) {\n        this.gameViewModel = gameViewModel;\n        this.setupViewModel = setupViewModel;\n        this.viewManagerModel = viewManagerModel;\n    }\n\n    @Override\n    public void prepareSuccessView(StartNewGameOutputData outputData) {\n        final GameRenderState render = gameViewModel.getState();\n        render.setBoard(GameViewModelMapper.toBoardRenderState(outputData.gameState()));\n        render.setStatus(GameViewModelMapper.toStatusRenderState(outputData.gameState()));\n        render.setMessage(null);\n        gameViewModel.firePropertyChanged();\n\n        viewManagerModel.setState(gameViewModel.getViewName());\n        viewManagerModel.firePropertyChanged();\n    }\n\n    @Override\n    public void prepareFailView(String error) {\n        setupViewModel.getState().setMessage(error);\n        setupViewModel.firePropertyChanged();\n    }\n\n    @Override\n    public void switchToSetupView() {\n        viewManagerModel.setState(setupViewModel.getViewName());\n        viewManagerModel.firePropertyChanged();\n    }\n}",

{
  "content": "package game.make_human_move.use_case;\n\nimport game.GameSessionDataAccess;\nimport game.GameSessionRules;\nimport game.domain.GameState;\nimport game.domain.exception.InvalidMoveException;\n\n/**\n * The Interactor for the Make Human Move Use Case. Reads the current game\n * from the application-layer session, applies the move, writes the updated\n * game back, and reports whether the AI is to move next. Moves that cannot\n * apply (no game in progress, the game is over, or it is the AI's turn) are\n * ignored without touching the presenter.\n */\npublic final class MakeHumanMoveInteractor implements MakeHumanMoveInputBoundary {\n\n    private final MakeHumanMoveOutputBoundary presenter;\n    private final GameSessionDataAccess session;\n\n    public MakeHumanMoveInteractor(\n            MakeHumanMoveOutputBoundary presenter,\n            GameSessionDataAccess session) {\n        this.presenter = presenter;\n        this.session = session;\n    }\n\n    @Override\n    public void execute(MakeHumanMoveInputData inputData) {\n        final GameState current = session.getCurrentGameState();\n        if (current == null || current.isGameOver() || GameSessionRules.isAiTurn(session.getMode(), current)) {\n            return;\n        }\n        try {\n            final GameState updated = current.applyMove(inputData.position());\n            session.setCurrentGameState(updated);\n            presenter.prepareSuccessView(new MakeHumanMoveOutputData(\n                    updated, GameSessionRules.isAiTurn(session.getMode(), updated)));\n        } catch (InvalidMoveException e) {\n            presenter.prepareFailView(e.getMessage());\n        }\n    }\n}",
  "filePath": "/Users/pgries/Projects/ca_examples/tictactoe/src/main/java/game/make_human_move/use_case/MakeHumanMoveInteractor.java"
}

{
  "content": "package game.request_ai_move;\n\nimport game.GameRenderState;\nimport game.GameSessionDataAccess;\nimport game.GameViewModel;\nimport game.GameViewModelMapper;\nimport game.request_ai_move.use_case.RequestAiMoveOutputBoundary;\nimport game.request_ai_move.use_case.RequestAiMoveOutputData;\nimport framework.UiScheduler;\n\n/**\n * The Presenter for the Request AI Move Use Case. Applies the AI move on the\n * UI thread, discarding the result if the session moved on (e.g. a restart)\n * while the move was being computed in the background; staleness is checked\n * against the base the result was computed from, which travels in the output\n * data.\n */\npublic class RequestAiMovePresenter implements RequestAiMoveOutputBoundary {\n\n    private final GameViewModel gameViewModel;\n    private final UiScheduler uiScheduler;\n    private final GameSessionDataAccess session;\n\n    public RequestAiMovePresenter(\n            GameViewModel gameViewModel,\n            UiScheduler uiScheduler,\n            GameSessionDataAccess session) {\n        this.gameViewModel = gameViewModel;\n        this.uiScheduler = uiScheduler;\n        this.session = session;\n    }\n\n    @Override\n    public void prepareSuccessView(RequestAiMoveOutputData outputData) {\n        uiScheduler.runOnUiThread(() -> {\n            if (session.getCurrentGameState().equals(outputData.base())) {\n                session.setCurrentGameState(outputData.updatedState());\n                final GameRenderState render = gameViewModel.getState();\n                render.setBoard(GameViewModelMapper.toBoardRenderState(outputData.updatedState()));\n                render.setStatus(GameViewModelMapper.toStatusRenderState(outputData.updatedState()));\n                render.setMessage(null);\n                gameViewModel.firePropertyChanged();\n            }\n        });\n    }\n\n    @Override\n    public void prepareFailView(String error) {\n        uiScheduler.runOnUiThread(() -> {\n            gameViewModel.getState().setMessage(error);\n            gameViewModel.firePropertyChanged();\n        });\n    }\n}",

{
  "content": "package game.save_game.use_case;\n\nimport game.GameSessionDataAccess;\nimport game.domain.GameState;\nimport game.domain.SavedGame;\nimport java.io.IOException;\n\n/**\n * The Interactor for the Save Game Use Case. Hands the session snapshot from\n * the application-layer session to the persistence boundary and routes\n * persistence failures through the output boundary, never to the view.\n */\npublic final class SaveGameInteractor implements SaveGameInputBoundary {\n\n    private final SaveGameOutputBoundary presenter;\n    private final SaveGameDataAccess saveGameDataAccess;\n    private final GameSessionDataAccess session;\n\n    public SaveGameInteractor(\n            SaveGameOutputBoundary presenter,\n            SaveGameDataAccess saveGameDataAccess,\n            GameSessionDataAccess session) {\n        this.presenter = presenter;\n        this.saveGameDataAccess = saveGameDataAccess;\n        this.session = session;\n    }\n\n    @Override\n    public void execute(SaveGameInputData inputData) {\n        final GameState state = session.getCurrentGameState();\n        if (state == null) {\n            presenter.prepareFailView(\"no game in progress to save\");\n            return;\n        }\n        try {\n            saveGameDataAccess.save(new SavedGame(state, session.getMode(), session.getDifficulty()));\n            presenter.prepareSuccessView(new SaveGameOutputData());\n        } catch (IOException e) {\n            presenter.prepareFailView(\"could not save the game: \" + e.getMessage());\n        }\n    }\n}",
  "filePath": "/Users/pgries/Projects/ca_examples/tictactoe/src/main/java/game/save_game/use_case/SaveGameInteractor.java"
}
