  "content": "package game.load_game.use_case;\n\nimport game.GameSessionDataAccess;\nimport game.domain.SavedGame;\nimport java.io.IOException;\nimport java.util.Optional;\n\n/**\n * The Interactor for the Load Game Use Case. Loads the saved session through\n * the persistence boundary, restores it as the application-layer session,\n * and routes \"no saved game\" and persistence failures through the output\n * boundary, never to the view.\n */\npublic final class LoadGameInteractor implements LoadGameInputBoundary {\n\n    private final LoadGameOutputBoundary presenter;\n    private final LoadGameDataAccess loadGameDataAccess;\n    private final GameSessionDataAccess session;\n\n    public LoadGameInteractor(\n            LoadGameOutputBoundary presenter,\n            LoadGameDataAccess loadGameDataAccess,\n            GameSessionDataAccess session) {\n        this.presenter = presenter;\n        this.loadGameDataAccess = loadGameDataAccess;\n        this.session = session;\n    }\n\n    @Override\n    public void execute(LoadGameInputData inputData) {\n        try {\n            Optional<SavedGame> savedGame = loadGameDataAccess.load();\n            if (savedGame.isEmpty()) {\n                presenter.prepareFailView(\"no saved game found\");\n            } else {\n                SavedGame game = savedGame.get();\n                session.setCurrentGame(game.gameState(), game.mode(), game.difficulty());\n                presenter.prepareSuccessView(new LoadGameOutputData(game));\n            }\n        } catch (IOException e) {\n            presenter.prepareFailView(\"could not load the saved game: \" + e.getMessage());\n        }\n    }\n}",

  "content": "package game.load_game;\n\nimport framework.ViewManagerModel;\nimport game.GameRenderState;\nimport game.GameViewModel;\nimport game.GameViewModelMapper;\nimport game.domain.SavedGame;\nimport game.load_game.use_case.LoadGameOutputBoundary;\nimport game.load_game.use_case.LoadGameOutputData;\nimport game.setup.SetupViewModel;\n\n/**\n * The Presenter for the Load Game Use Case. Renders the restored game from\n * the output data and navigates to the game screen on success; failures go\n * to the setup view model, whose view shows them. The session itself was\n * restored by the interactor.\n */\npublic class LoadGamePresenter implements LoadGameOutputBoundary {\n\n    private final GameViewModel gameViewModel;\n    private final SetupViewModel setupViewModel;\n    private final ViewManagerModel viewManagerModel;\n\n    public LoadGamePresenter(\n            GameViewModel gameViewModel,\n            SetupViewModel setupViewModel,\n            ViewManagerModel viewManagerModel) {\n        this.gameViewModel = gameViewModel;\n        this.setupViewModel = setupViewModel;\n        this.viewManagerModel = viewManagerModel;\n    }\n\n    @Override\n    public void prepareSuccessView(LoadGameOutputData outputData) {\n        final SavedGame savedGame = outputData.savedGame();\n        final GameRenderState render = gameViewModel.getState();\n        render.setBoard(GameViewModelMapper.toBoardRenderState(savedGame.gameState()));\n        render.setStatus(GameViewModelMapper.toStatusRenderState(savedGame.gameState()));\n        render.setMessage(null);\n        gameViewModel.firePropertyChanged();\n\n        viewManagerModel.setState(gameViewModel.getViewName());\n        viewManagerModel.firePropertyChanged();\n    }\n\n    @Override\n    public void prepareFailView(String error) {\n        setupViewModel.getState().setMessage(error);\n        setupViewModel.firePropertyChanged();\n    }\n}",

gameViewModel = new GameViewModel();\n        PropertyChangeListener listener = evt -> fireCount++;\n        gameViewModel.addPropertyChangeListener(listener);\n        presenter = new MakeHumanMovePresenter(gameViewModel, () -> requestAiMoveCalls++);\n    }\n\n    @Test\n    void prepareSuccessView_UpdatesViewModelAndFires() {\n        game.domain.GameState updated = assertThat(gameViewModel.getState().getStatus().message()).isEqualTo(\"O's turn\");\n        assertThat(fireCount).isEqualTo(1);\n        assertThat(requestAiMoveCalls).isZero();\n    }\n\n    @Test\n    void prepareSuccessView_AiToMoveNext_RequestsAiMove() {\n        game.domain.GameState afterHumanMove = game.domain.GameState.newGame(CONFIG_3X3)\n            .applyMove(new Position(0, 0));\n\n        presenter.prepareSuccessView(new MakeHumanMoveOutputData(afterHumanMove, true));\n\n        assertThat(requestAiMoveCalls).isEqualTo(1);\n    }\n\n    @Test\n    void Key observations so far:

1. **Main location**: CAWithBuilder has `app/Main.java` (thin, in `app` package); tictactoe has `framework/Main.java`. Also tictactoe's Main uses SwingUtilities.invokeLater; CAWithBuilder's Main calls build(), pack(), setVisible(true) directly. Also CAWithBuilder calls `application.pack()` in Main, tictactoe doesn't pack.

2. **AppBuilder API**: CAWithBuilder has per-component methods `addSignupView()`, `addLoginView()`, `addChangePasswordView()`, `addSignupUseCase()`, `addLoginUseCase()`, `addChangePasswordUseCase()`, each returning `this` (fluent builder), and `build()` returns JFrame. tictactoe has a single `build()` that does everything, no add* methods, returns `MainFrame` (a JFrame subclass presumably). The AGENTS.md says "Wiring in `app/AppBuilder` (per-frame wiring methods)". CAWithBuilder's per-frame wiring = add*View/add*UseCase methods.

3. **ViewModel API**: CAWithBuilder's ViewModel has `firePropertyChanged(String propertyName)` overload; tictactoe's ViewModel lacks that overload. That's a delta that matters for teaching (ChangePasswordView listens for multiple property names).

4. **ViewManager / ViewManagerModel**: CAWithBuilder has `framework/ViewManager.java` and `framework/ViewManagerModel.java`; tictactoe has neither — no ViewManager infrastructure, no CardLayout-based navigation between views (it's a single MainFrame). Let me check MainFrame — is it a JFrame with CardLayout? The AppBuilder imports java.awt.CardLayout but doesn't use it... 21:     public static BoardViewModel toBoardViewModel(GameState state) {
22:         int size = state.config().boardSize();
23:         List<CellViewModel> cells = new ArrayList<>(size * size);
24:         for (int row = 0; row < size; row++) {
25:             for (int column = 0; column < size; column++) {
26:                 Position position = new Position(row, column);
27:                 CellSymbol symbol = state.board().get(position)
28:                     .map(mark -> mark == Mark.X ? CellSymbol.X : CellSymbol.O)
29:                     .orElse(CellSymbol.EMPTY);
30:                 cells.add(new CellViewModel(position, symbol));
31:             }
32:         }
33:         List<Position> winningLine = state.status() instanceof Win win
34:             ? win.winningLine()
35:             : List.of();
36:         return new BoardViewModel(size, cells, winningLine, outcomeKindOf(state));
37:     }
38: 
39:     public static StatusViewModel toStatusViewModel(GameState state) {
40:         String message;
41:         if (state.status() instanceof Win win) {
42:             message = win.winner() + " wins!";
43:         } else if (state.status() instanceof Draw) {
44:             message = "Draw!";
45:         } else {
46:             message = state.currentTurn() + "'s turn";
47:         }
48:         return new StatusViewModel(message, outcomeKindOf(state));
49:     }

4. **No ViewManager/ViewManagerModel navigation infrastructure; navigation handled by view calling frame directly** — CAWithBuilder: framework/ViewManager.java + framework/ViewManagerModel.java; presenters set state on ViewManagerModel (viewManagerModel.setState(getViewName()) + firePropertyChanged) and ViewManager switches CardLayout; views expose getViewName(). tictactoe: MainFrame has its own CardLayout with hard-coded card names, and SetupPanel calls mainFrame.showGameScreen() directly after controller.execute (view-driven navigation); presenters never navigate. This is a teaching-relevant delta about who controls navigation.

5. **ViewModel base missing firePropertyChanged(String) overload** — CAWithBuilder framework/ViewModel.java has both firePropertyChanged() and firePropertyChanged(String propertyName); ChangePasswordPresenter uses firePropertyChanged("password") and ChangePasswordView distinguishes events by property name. tictactoe framework/ViewModel.java only has the no-arg version. Also viewName is vestigial in tictactoe (MainFrame never uses getViewName()).

MainFrame.setControllers(...) wires two controllers into panels; the reference's AppBuilder calls view.setXController(...).

7. **Main placement and content: framework/Main vs app/Main** — CAWithBuilder app/Main.java: builds via fluent chain, calls pack(), setVisible(true) on the JFrame returned by build(). tictactoe framework/Main.java: build().setVisible(true) inside SwingUtilities.invokeLater; no pack(). Minor but structural (entry point in framework vs app package).

8. **build() return type: JFrame vs MainFrame subclass; AppBuilder holds view instances vs not** — minor, could fold into #1.

9. **InputData/OutputData: records with public accessors vs classes with getters** — CAWithBuilder uses plain classes (SignupInputData, SignupOutputData with getUsername() etc., some package-private getters); tictactoe uses records. Teaching-relevant? The reference also uses immutable data classes with getters; records are a fine modern equivalent. Probably a low-priority "note" — maybe mention briefly. The user said avoid stylistic; records vs classes is borderline but I'll include as a minor note since it changes the API shape (public accessor names, equals/hashCode semantics).

10. **Boundary naming matches** — both use <UseCase>InputBoundary etc. Aligned; no delta. But note the reference's InputBoundary sometimes carries extra navigation methods (SignupInputBoundary.switchToLoginView) — tictactoe's are execute-only. Is this a delta? It's a delta in boundary surface, but AGENTS.md for tictactoe only requires execute. The user asked "do the reference's names match exactly" — names match. The extra method is a difference worth a one-liner.

11. **No data access layer at all** — CAWithBuilder has per-use-case DAO interfaces in use_case packages (SignupUserDataAccessInterface, LoginUserDataAccessInterface, ChangePasswordUserDataAccessInterface) + data_access/ package with implementations (DBUserDataAccessObject, FileUserDataAccessObject, InMemoryUserDataAccessObject). tictactoe has no DAO interfaces in use_case packages and no data_access package. Not applicable for a stateless game, but it's a structural delta vs the reference (the boundary-set in the reference includes a 6th member per use case). Worth listing as "not applicable / absent" so the teacher knows.

12. **CommonUser/CommonUserFactory-style entity+factory pattern** — CAWithBuilder user/User.java (interface), user/UserFactory.java (interface), user/CommonUser.java, user/CommonUserFactory.java. tictactoe domain is concrete classes (game/domain/*) and GameStateFactory is a static utility with private constructor, not an injectable factory interface. The factory-interface injection pattern (as taught by CommonUserFactory) is absent. This ties to #3.

13. **UiScheduler**: reference has none (all synchronous); tictactoe adds framework/UiScheduler + framework/ui/SwingUiScheduler. This is an extension beyond the reference — not a misalignment, but note that in the reference, presenters/interactors are all synchronous and there's no stale-result discard concept. The user asked "UI scheduler handling?" — answer: reference has none; tictactoe's is an addition. No change needed, but the presenter for RequestAiMove takes UiScheduler while other presenters don't (asymmetry — fine).

Also: presenter construction args: reference presenters take (ViewManagerModel, ...ViewModel(s)) — multi-viewmodels + navigation model. tictactoe presenters take GameViewModel (+ UiScheduler / Runnable handoff). The Runnable handoff (MakeHumanMovePresenter takes Runnable requestAiMove wired to controller::execute) is a tictactoe-specific wiring mechanism — worth a note as it's a cross-use-case coupling done via AppBuilder (consistent with AGENTS.md's "cross-cutting logic belongs in the frame"... actually the Runnable handoff is a presenter-to-controller link, notable).

CAWithBuilder distinguishes: presentation states are <UseCase>State (SignupState, LoginState, ChangePasswordState) and the domain entity is User. The name collision is confusing for teaching. Worth listing as a notable delta.

Also the tictactoe presentation bean holds domain objects (game.domain.GameState currentGameState, AiStrategy) directly — the presentation layer depends on domain types. In CAWithBuilder, SignupState holds only primitives/Strings; the presenter maps OutputData (which contains domain-ish data) into the state. Actually LoginPresenter sets username (a String) into ChangePasswordState — the state holds primitives only. In tictactoe, GameState (presentation) holds domain GameState + AiStrategy + BoardViewModel etc. That's a structural delta: presentation bean vs domain model separation. The reference's ViewModel state never references domain entities; tictactoe's does. Worth reporting: "presentation bean holds domain types (domain GameState, AiStrategy) — reference states hold only view primitives."

That's a good teaching point: the shared bean in tictactoe mixes render data, session data, AND the domain aggregate; CAWithBuilder's State classes are pure view state (strings/errors).

## Deltas (tictactoe vs CAWithBuilder)

### 1. AppBuilder has no per-frame wiring methods — everything is in one `build()`
- Reference: `/Users/pgries/Projects/ca_examples/CAWithBuilder/src/main/java/app/AppBuilder.java` has `addSignupView()`, `addLoginView()`, `addChangePasswordView()`, `addSignupUseCase()`, `addLoginUseCase()`, `addChangePasswordUseCase()`, each returning `this` (fluent), plus a final `build()` that returns a plain `JFrame`. Fields hold the views/view-models; each `add*UseCase()` constructs Presenter → Interactor → Controller and calls `view.setXController(...)`.
- Target: `/Users/pgries/Projects/ca_examples/tictactoe/src/main/java/app/AppBuilder.java` has only `build()`; everything is local to that method, only `gameViewModel` is a field, and it returns the concrete `MainFrame` subclass. This contradicts the "per-frame wiring methods" convention in AGENTS.md.

### 2. Controllers are not thin — they hold extra dependencies and mutate session state
- Reference: all three controllers (`SignupController`, `LoginController`, `ChangePasswordController` in `account/*/` and `authentication/login/`) take **only** the `InputBoundary` and only build `InputData` from primitives.
- Target: controllers take extra collaborators and do use-case work before calling the interactor:
  - `game/start_new_game/StartNewGameController.java` — takes `AiStrategyFactory` + `GameViewModel`, sets `mode`/`aiStrategy` on the shared `GameState`, and caches `lastInput` for `restart()`.
  - `game/make_human_move/MakeHumanMoveController.java` — takes `GameViewModel` and performs the game-over / AI-turn guard (use-case policy) in the controller.
  - `game/request_ai_move/RequestAiMoveController.java` — takes `GameViewModel` + `UiScheduler`, sets `pendingAiBase`, and runs the interactor on a background thread.

### 3. Strategy/factory instantiation point: controller-held factory + strategy smuggled via InputData, vs interactor-injected factory
- Reference: `user/CommonUserFactory.java` implements `UserFactory`; the AppBuilder creates it and injects it into the **interactor constructor** (`account/signup/use_case/SignupInteractor.java` calls `userFactory.create(...)`).
- Target: `game/ai/AiStrategyFactory.java` is injected into `StartNewGameController` (not the interactor), and the resulting `AiStrategy` is stored in the shared presentation bean and later passed into the use case through `game/request_ai_move/use_case/RequestAiMoveInputData.java` (record carrying `AiStrategy`). The interactors never see the factory. In the reference, external collaborators enter the use case via constructor injection at the boundary, not via input data.

### 4. Presentation bean holds domain types; class-name collision `GameState`
- Reference: per-use-case state beans (`account/signup/SignupState.java`, `authentication/login/LoginState.java`, `account/change_password/ChangePasswordState.java`) hold **only view primitives** (Strings, errors); the domain entity is `user/User.java` — clearly separated.
- Target: `game/GameState.java` (presentation) holds the domain aggregate `game.domain.GameState` plus `game.ai.AiStrategy`, and `game/GameState.java` vs `game/domain/GameState.java` are two classes with the same name in sibling packages — confusing in teaching. The presentation layer here reaches directly into domain types.

### 5. No ViewManager / ViewManagerModel; navigation is view-driven instead of presenter-driven
- Reference: `framework/ViewManager.java` (a `PropertyChangeListener` on the `ViewManagerModel` that switches a `CardLayout`) and `framework/ViewManagerModel.java` (`extends ViewModel<String>`). Presenters navigate by `viewManagerModel.setState(<viewName>)` + `firePropertyChanged()` (e.g. `SignupPresenter.prepareSuccessView`). Views expose `getViewName()`.
- Target: no ViewManager or ViewManagerModel anywhere. `framework/ui/MainFrame.java` owns a private `CardLayout` with hard-coded card names, and navigation happens when `SetupPanel.onStartClicked()` calls `mainFrame.showGameScreen()` directly — the view controls navigation, and `StartNewGamePresenter` never navigates.

### 6. `framework/ViewModel` base is missing the `firePropertyChanged(String)` overload
- Reference: `/Users/pgries/Projects/ca_examples/CAWithBuilder/src/main/java/framework/ViewModel.java` has both `firePropertyChanged()` and `firePropertyChanged(String propertyName)`; `ChangePasswordPresenter` fires `"password"` and `ChangePasswordView.propertyChange` distinguishes events by name.
- Target: `/Users/pgries/Projects/ca_examples/tictactoe/src/main/java/framework/ViewModel.java` has only the no-arg version. Also, the `viewName` field is vestigial — `MainFrame` never calls `getViewName()`.

### 7. Views live in `framework/ui`; no per-capability View classes
- Reference: one View per capability inside the capability package — `account/signup/SignupView.java`, `authentication/login/LoginView.java`, `account/change_password/ChangePasswordView.java` — each a `JPanel` implementing `PropertyChangeListener` with `getViewName()` and `setXController(...)`; only shared Swing widgets (`framework/LabelTextPanel.java`) sit in `framework`.
- Target: all UI is in `framework/ui/` (`MainFrame.java`, `SetupPanel.java`, `BoardPanel.java`, `StatusPanel.java`, `EffectOverlayPanel.java`, `Theme.java`); the per-capability View layer is absent and the capability packages contain only Controller/Presenter. AppBuilder wires via `frame.setControllers(...)` instead of per-view `setXController(...)`.

### 8. `Main` placement and content differ
- Reference: `/Users/pgries/Projects/ca_examples/CAWithBuilder/src/main/java/app/Main.java` — in the `app` package, chains `add*View()/add*UseCase()`, then `pack()` + `setVisible(true)`, no EDT wrapper.
- Target: `/Users/pgries/Projects/ca_examples/tictactoe/src/main/java/framework/Main.java` — in `framework`, uses `SwingUtilities.invokeLater` and never calls `pack()` (size is fixed in the `MainFrame` constructor). Entry point in the framework layer vs the app layer.

### 9. No per-use-case data-access interface / `data_access` layer
- Reference: each use_case package includes a DAO interface (`SignupUserDataAccessInterface`, `LoginUserDataAccessInterface`, `ChangePasswordUserDataAccessInterface`) and `data_access/` holds implementations (`DBUserDataAccessObject`, `FileUserDataAccessObject`, `InMemoryUserDataAccessObject`); AppBuilder constructs one DAO and shares it across interactors.
- Target: no DAO interfaces in the `use_case` packages and no `data_access` package at all (the game has nothing to persist, but the reference's "sixth boundary member + separate implementation layer" pattern is absent and should at least be acknowledged in teaching).

### 10. Domain entity/factory pattern: concrete classes + static factory vs interface + injectable factory
- Reference: `user/User.java` (interface), `user/UserFactory.java` (interface), `user/CommonUser.java`, `user/CommonUserFactory.java` — the "CommonUser/CommonUserFactory" pattern from AGENTS.md, instantiated in AppBuilder and injected.
- Target: `game/domain/*` are concrete classes and `game/domain/GameStateFactory.java` is a static utility (private constructor, `GameStateFactory.newGame(...)` called from `StartNewGameInteractor`). No factory interface, no injectable instance.

### 11. InputData/OutputData: records vs plain classes (minor, but visible API shape)
- Reference: `SignupInputData`, `SignupOutputData`, etc. are plain classes with getters (some package-private, e.g. `getUsername()` in `SignupInputData`).
- Target: all six data objects are Java records with public accessors and value semantics (`StartNewGameInputData`, `MakeHumanMoveInputData`, `RequestAiMoveInputData`, and the three OutputData records).

## Points you asked about that are already aligned (no action)

- **Boundary naming**: reference uses `SignupInputBoundary` / `SignupInputData` / `SignupInteractor` / `SignupOutputBoundary` / `SignupOutputData`; tictactoe matches exactly (`StartNewGame*`, `MakeHumanMove*`, `RequestAiMove*`). One small surface difference: the reference's `SignupInputBoundary`/`SignupOutputBoundary` carry an extra `switchToLoginView()` method; tictactoe boundaries are `execute` / `prepareSuccessView` / `prepareFailView` only.
- **Interactor construction**: both projects pass the `OutputBoundary` to the interactor **in the constructor** — no setter in the reference (`new SignupInteractor(dao, outputBoundary, factory)`, `new LoginInteractor(dao, outputBoundary)`).
- **UiScheduler**: the reference has none (fully synchronous, single-threaded Swing); tictactoe's `framework/UiScheduler` + `framework/ui/SwingUiScheduler` with stale-result discard is a deliberate extension beyond the reference, not a misalignment. Note the asymmetry: `RequestAiMovePresenter` takes the `UiScheduler` but `StartNewGamePresenter`/`MakeHumanMovePresenter` don't.
